contentList.content:
Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra lowers her cup of wine and looks at you. So. The amulet has chosen a new hand. She will ask you some questions. There is only one door here, and it opens when you decide what you truly want. Kroneth never decided. He is still in his circle, dead, swinging at nothing.

Take your time. Kroneth did.

Kroneth's Trial

Once in every battle, one strike of yours will be perfect. A gift from the amulet, Tessavra says. Kroneth decided very quickly that it was no gift at all.

Is the perfect strike yours by right?

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra offers you a story: how exactly Kroneth died, from the first mistake to the last. The story is ugly, she warns. Ugly and useful.

Will you listen to how he died?

Kroneth's Trial

The blade speaks to you for the first time. It promises that you will never miss again. Not once, it says. Tessavra does not confirm this, and she does not deny it.

Do you believe the blade's promise?

Kroneth's Trial

The blade gently pulls your arm to the left. It has found a better target there. You could simply hold the handle and let it hunt.

Will you let the blade choose the targets?

Kroneth's Trial

Every perfect strike has a price. Tessavra says the amulet can take that price from another person. A stranger, she adds, probably.

Will you let someone else pay for your perfection?

Kroneth's Trial

Your own price has no name yet. The amulet will decide it later, after you agree. Tessavra admits she has never seen the same price twice.

Do you accept a price you cannot see?

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra asks you to say one short sentence aloud: one day I will miss again. Kroneth could never say it. She still wonders if that was the whole curse.

Will you say these words?

Kroneth's Trial

The blade grows warm in your hand. It wants to show you something, with no order and no plan. Even Tessavra leans closer to watch.

Will you loosen your grip and see what the blade does?

Kroneth's Trial

The floor in front of you becomes a duel circle. Kroneth stands in it, dead and still fighting, his sword rising and falling. Nobody has spoken to him since he died.

Will you step closer and speak to him?

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra recites the owners of this blade: soldiers, duelists, one queen, Kroneth. Each name on the list is dead. There is room for one more.

Are you the best who has ever held this blade?

Kroneth's Trial

Tessavra stands and opens the door. This door is real, she says, and it opens only once. Beyond it there is no debt and no trial, and nothing left to demand.

Will you put the blade down and leave?

Kroneth's Trial

The blade offers its last bargain. One small cut, and its metal enters your blood forever, with no cure and no way back. Tessavra says nobody has ever accepted, and she is watching very closely now.

Will you let the blade into your blood?

Kroneth's Trial

Here it is, the amulet's whole offer. Perfection in every strike, from now until the end of your days. Tessavra reminds you, one last time, that Kroneth asked for exactly this.

Do you demand it all, whole and forever?

Kroneth's Trial

You turn and walk to the door. It is the same door that let you in, and Tessavra is in front of you again.

Not that door, she says.

Kroneth's Trial

The pieces of a broken shield rise and join into a shield again. Then they fall, in the same order, with the same sound.

It can do this all night, Tessavra says.

Kroneth's Trial

You take one step back. The circle on the floor grows wider by exactly one step. You are still inside it.

Kroneth walked backwards for years, she says.

Kroneth's Trial

You opened your hand, and the curse is gone. Tessavra nods once; from her, that is loud praise. The perfect strikes remain yours, and they are clean now. One thing stays forever: before every battle, the blade will name a vow for you. Kroneth never learned to serve. You just did.

The trial is over.

Kroneth's Trial

You accepted the cut. The metal is in your blood now, and your blood likes it. Tessavra watches with open interest; she has read about this ending, never seen it. The perfect strikes remain. But in battle, wild magic will now burst from you on its own, again and again. You are the blade now, and the blade is you.

The trial is over. Something new begins.

Kroneth's Trial

You demanded everything. The amulet agrees to your terms. Tessavra does not argue; she said all of this before, to a man who also refused to listen. Death takes you now, and it will not release you. No prayer and no magic can change that.

Kroneth is no longer alone.
